decisions.scan_shows: A dark vertical curving brace lies immediately left of the first two Roman numerals; it bends outward to the left between their baselines and returns to the second line. Its upper part crowds the first numeral. H describes this graphic only.

The upper and lower horizontal strokes enclose a broad descending/rising central form and a distinct right upright. An extra narrow central trace merges with the thick retracing and adjacent brace, so VI is preferred but VII remains possible. No separate earlier numeral can be read from the overtracing. The C doubt is retained unchanged; H gives uncertainty on VI alone and omits the transverse rules, so the extra VII candidate is a substantive uncertainty difference.

There are two detached small marks: an upper oblique dash and a lower near-oval mark. The lower mark has a pale centre but no securely separable right stem. Their vertical separation favours a colon, while the lower loop and upper slant still allow a compact à. The retained alternatives are reordered from C; H gives an unqualified colon.

A low initial a and long p descender are followed by compressed r/e strokes and a separate curled final s. A very faint detached short slant stands above the middle of the word; it favours a grave accent but is too faint to exclude unaccented apres. The preferred alternative is changed from C, and uncertainty is retained against H’s certain après.

notes: This is one sheet of handwritten planning notes on a printed INSTITUT DES HAUTES ÉTUDES SCIENTIFIQUES letterhead. An encircled SGA 7 label sits beside two pairs of bracketed entries. The first entry juxtaposes decimal references and asks whether to redo 1.14. The second mentions an appendice and la lettre Deligne 2 pages; the phrase 2 pages is the author’s wording, not a page count independently verified here. The lower entries concern torsion, crystalline cohomology and comments on their relations, with a slanted question about making an exposé XXIII. The author’s explicit question marks occur twice in the first entry, once in parentheses beside XXII and once after the margin numeral. No date, manuscript page number, signature or formal title is visible; SGA 7 functions as the page’s label. The archive number 76 is recorded only as a comment. The first Roman numeral is heavily retraced; no independently legible underlying cancelled text is established. No other cancellation or insertion is visible. Four reader uncertainties remain in place: first Roman numeral VI/VII, colon/à connector, faint accent in après/apres, and relation/relations. Source and crop delivery details are in processing.json; every requested image reached the context on its first delivery.
math_reading_decisions: All unmarked C-context numeral targets were inspected: second-entry VI, lower XXI, lower XXII and marginal XXIII each have upper and lower transverse strokes. The first numeral retains VI/VII uncertainty.

The decimal references 1.11, the following 1.14, 1.15, terminal 1.22 and Refaire 1.14 were read separately. The small last digit of the second reference was inspected in its sole crop and is the open handwritten 4; no uncertainty is added there.
The stroke between 1.15 and 1.22 is one short unheaded horizontal dash. There is no arrowhead. The terminal 1.22 was settled by half a, so it was not cropped.
Both free questions in the first entry, the parenthesized (?) beside XXII and the marginal question mark are preserved, with the parentheses independently visible in the half.
The shortened coh. has a separate low period after h. The en cohomologie continuation is part of the third entry, while relations avec coh. cristalline. belongs to the fourth.
The two braces and loop are graphic grouping marks, reproduced by the existing C TikZ paths. H describes those three graphics without rendering them; those differences are reported individually.
No mathematical assertion was proved, re-proved or used as a theorem. These were reference-glyph and layout readings, so no mathematical check event is recorded.
